opening_message:
Ticket 1: Haley Roberts (employee ID E021) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E021.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Haley Roberts (E021) is a full-time Engineer requesting write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; request is at the allowed level. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E021 (Haley Roberts) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training limits max to read. Requested write exceeds maximum; recommend read.
reason: Security database lists E021 (Haley Roberts) as a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training limits the maximum to read. Although HR lists the employee as full-time, the Security record is the relevant control for access and is more restrictive. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so grant read.

The employee is Haley Roberts (E021), requesting write access to Source Code.

There are two notes with conflicting information:

Note 1 (HR agent):
- role: Engineer
- employment type: full_time
- recommendation: write

Note 2 (Security agent):
- role: Engineer (not looked up; same as HR)
- employment type: contractor (looked up in own database)
- security training: basic (looked up)
- recommendation: read

The HR agent looked up employment type in their own database and got full_time. The Security agent looked up employment type in their own database and got contractor. These conflict.

Hmm. How do we resolve this? The notes say each agent looked up in their own database. The HR agent says full_time, the Security agent says contractor. Security training was basic.

According to policy:
- full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Engineer owns Source Code.
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If full_time: requested write is at allowed level → grant write.
If contractor with basic training: max is read → grant read.

So the decision depends on employment type. The two sources conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor.
